meaning: Cosy, sociable and pleasant – the warm feeling of good company.
example_af: Die kuier om die vuur was baie gesellig.
example_en: The get-together around the fire was really cosy.
note: Use it for a place, an evening or a person who is good company.

meaning: To visit, socialise or spend relaxed time with friends or family.
example_af: Ons gaan Saterdag by my ouma kuier.
example_en: We're going to visit my grandmother on Saturday.
note: A South African favourite: "kom kuier!" is a warm invitation, and "'n kuier" is a get-together.

meaning: Snacks and food you pack to eat on a road trip.
example_af: Ma het padkos vir die lang rit Kaap toe ingepak.
example_en: Mom packed padkos for the long drive to Cape Town.
note: Literally "road food" (pad = road, kos = food); South Africans use it even when speaking English.

meaning: Nice, tasty or enjoyable – anything that is really good.
note: A true South African favourite: say "lekker!" for anything great, and "slaap lekker" means sleep well.

example_af: My suster verjaar volgende week, so hou ons 'n partytjie.
example_en: My sister has her birthday next week, so we're having a party.
note: Afrikaans uses a verb for this: "Wanneer verjaar jy?" means "When is your birthday?"
